title: Chocolate Mousse
subtitle: Classic French dark chocolate mousse
excerpt: A light, airy chocolate mousse made from dark chocolate, eggs, and cream. No gelatine, no cream cheese. Sets in four hours in the fridge and unmistakably tastes of chocolate.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chocolate mousse in its modern French form, with separated eggs and whipped whites, is documented in French cookbooks from the eighteenth century. The dish was codified as a restaurant classic in the twentieth century and became a standard of French home cooking.

recipeTools.notes: For whisking the egg whites and cream.

content.text: Chocolate mousse is dark chocolate melted and stirred through egg yolks, then lightened with whipped cream and folded egg whites. The texture should be light and airy, not dense like a ganache. The key is folding the whites in gently enough to keep the air in, but thoroughly enough that no white streaks remain.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks and half the sugar together in a bowl until pale and slightly thickened. Stir into the warm chocolate mixture with the salt.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. In a clean, dry bowl, whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the remaining sugar and whisk to stiff peaks.

Fold the whipped cream through the chocolate mixture until combined. Then add a third of the egg whites and stir in to loosen. Fold in the remaining whites in two additions with a large spoon, using a figure-of-eight motion to keep as much air as possible.
Divide between six glasses or ramekins. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set. Serve cold.
